about: Engines beside the screen (DESIGN 5.12, N5): an engine declared `beside the screen` runs where its canvas is drawn (`canvas ... runs Screen`), one instance per canvas, from when its window opens until it closes. It speaks the engine interface of conformance/engines.json and exports `clarity_tick` and `clarity_draw` besides it. At every frame the renderer calls `clarity_tick` with the milliseconds since the last frame (`[ms]`; the first frame gives 0), then `clarity_draw` (`[]`), whose value is the canvas's shapes in its units, as a draw handler's (conformance/drawing.json). With `on open` (`opens`), `clarity_open` runs once, when the instance is made, before the first frame. The renderer skips a frame while the engine is still busy with the last one, so frames never pile up. `engine` is screen.wasm, built from engines/screen: it draws a dot that moves 1 unit every 10 ms and the time it has run. `frames` gives the ticks in order and the shapes after each. A frame that fails, or runs longer than the engine's time limit, ends the engine: the canvas shows `fails` in place of its drawing, the renderer calls it no more, and the window works on. `fails` cases give the ticks before and the tick that fails. Pointer and keys on the canvas go to the engine when it exports `clarity_pointer` and `clarity_key` (each is optional; without it the renderer sends none of that). The renderer keeps what happens between frames and hands it over at the start of the next frame, in order, before `clarity_tick`: `clarity_pointer` takes `[kind, x, y]`, kind `down`, `move` or `up`, in the canvas's units rounded down as a click is (conformance/drawing.json); `clarity_key` takes `[kind, key]`, kind `down` or `up`. `down` is the primary button or a touch going down on the drawing; while it is down the canvas keeps the pointer, so `move` and `up` beside the drawing are at its nearest edge (`near`). `move` is sent while the pointer is over the drawing or down. Moves in a row keep only the last (`queued`). A key is sent once when it goes down, not again while it repeats, and once when it comes up; when the canvas loses the keyboard, every key still down comes up. Only the keys of `keys` are sent, by those names: a letter as itself in lower case, a digit, and the named keys. `input` gives each frame's input, its ticks and the shapes after: screen.wasm moves its dot to where the pointer went down and drags it while down, and says which keys are down. Tells and hears: the answer of any call may carry `tells`, a list of `{"tell": name, "values": [...]}`, which the canvas hands to the window in order once the frame is drawn, each running the handler wired to it (`on finished: gameOver`) with its values. A hear (`sky.start(2)` in a handler) comes back with the handler's reply and waits, as input does, for the next frame: `{"hear": name, "values": [...]}` calls the engine's function of that name with the values. A hear is kept even before the engine is ready; a refused hear ends the engine as a failed frame does. `tells` gives each frame's input, tick, what it tells and its shapes: screen.wasm tells `lap` each time its dot comes round and `finished` with its time when Escape goes down, and hears `start(level)`, which starts it again at that level. Services: `uses` names those the engine uses, as in conformance/engines.json; beside the screen they are the renderer's, and a line the engine logs goes into the application's log, the standard error, where the backend's engines write. On the web stacks the page hands the line to the shell with the command `log_line` (`{"line": text}`), which writes it there. `logs` gives a frame's input and the lines the engine logs: screen.wasm logs `level N` when it hears `start(N)`.
name: Screen

frames.name: opened, it draws the time it has run
without on open, clarity_open does not run

fails.name: a frame the engine refuses
fails.fails: engine Screen failed in clarity_tick: a frame of more than ten seconds

fails.name: a frame that runs past the time limit
fails.fails: engine Screen failed in clarity_tick: it ran longer than 1 second

fails.name: a hear the engine refuses
fails.fails: engine Screen failed in start: a level is a whole number

input.name: the dot goes where the pointer goes down, and follows it while down

tells.name: a tick tells each lap, a hear starts it again, a key tells it finished

logs.name: it logs the level a hear starts it at
